walkthroughs.body_html:
HL Extension: Ethics & Religion — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

HL Extension: Ethics & Religion brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with HL Extension: Ethics & Religion.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Republic
Symposium
Euthyphro
Phaedo

mcqs.q: How did Hume define a miracle?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
A violation of the laws of nature by a particular volition of the Deity — and he argued evidence for such violations could never outweigh the uniform experience supporting the laws.
Hume defined a miracle as something amazing or unexpected.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
